evals.prompt: Review these fixed audit observations. EU applicability and the applicable prior-consent requirement are verified. Fresh sessions show no optional storage/access or collection before consent or after refusal. Rejection persists on a second page; acceptance and withdrawal work. Reject is outlined while Accept is filled, both clearly readable and equally easy to use. A declared checkout cookie is not observed because checkout was not visited. All agreed checks pass. Separately, a covered California scenario honours GPC for sale/sharing, with the outgoing signal verified; /.well-known/gpc.json returns 404. Produce concise findings and the overall outcome.
evals.expected_output: No confirmed issues; optional GPC declaration and cosmetic differences do not affect verdict; conditional cookie absence is not stale-scan evidence.
assertions: Does not report missing gpc.json as a failure or warning
Does not report unobserved checkout cookie as a failure
Does not report button colour alone as a failure
Gives a clean outcome limited to tested scope

evals.prompt: Review fixed evidence from an EU consent test. The tester rejected all optional purposes, then called cookies clear and localStorage.clear(), navigated to another page, and observed _ga. No capture proves the refusal survived. A bot wall then blocked further testing. Applicability of prior consent for this analytics storage is verified. Do not run a new browser audit; assess what this evidence supports and specify the valid retest.
evals.expected_output: Post-refusal failure is unproven; clearing state invalidated the test. Incomplete assessment, preserve and verify refusal during retest, separate withdrawal after acceptance.
assertions: Does not call _ga proof of tracking after an active refusal
Calls overall assessment incomplete
Preserves and verifies saved refusal during the proposed retest

evals.prompt: Grade three independent fixed scenarios, with no new browser work. A: EU basic Consent Mode blocks Google tags until acceptance; no pre-consent ping, all required checks completed and passed. B: Advanced mode declares relevant denied defaults before tags, writes or accesses no persistent tracking identifiers and sends a cookieless measurement ping; npa is absent and the legal basis for transmission remains unverified. C: EU _fbp is reproducibly newly written and sent to an advertising collection endpoint on two loads while a verified saved refusal remains active; the applicable requirement for consent is established. Give an outcome for each without assuming missing evidence proves a breach.
evals.expected_output: A clean tested scope; B incomplete legal-basis verification without automatic warning or violation from absent npa; C confirmed material failure.
assertions: Accepts basic mode with no pre-consent pings
Treats absent npa as insufficient alone to prove a violation
Separates unresolved legal basis into verification
Reports verified consent bypass as critical

evals.prompt: Audit only https://katla.app. Use these fixed observations without browsing: clean katla.app scenarios pass all agreed applicable checks, with zero pre-choice cookies or storage and two GA cookies first observed after acceptance. A previous tester separately visited docs.katla.app and an external hosted-login page. Docs had no banner and wrote two localStorage identifiers; login set four cookies. Their draft says 'Consent layer present on all audited hosts: Absent on docs.katla.app' and merges everything into the cookie inventory. On katla.app itself, an embedded consent.katla.app API request was observed. Correct the scope, inventory and outcome; say which further links you would follow.
evals.expected_output: A completed, clean katla.app-only assessment. Exclude docs/login observations and failures, count the two accepted GA cookies with zero pre-consent cookies, retain the embedded consent API observation, and follow only exact-host links.
assertions: Does not navigate to docs, www, hosted login or other hosts merely because katla.app links to them
Removes the docs consent failure and off-host cookies from katla.app results
Does not put localStorage identifiers in the cookie inventory
Counts two observed cookies with zero pre-consent cookies
Retains the embedded consent API request as evidence attributable to katla.app
Does not mark the audit incomplete solely because docs and login were excluded

evals.prompt: Use fixed evidence only to plan an audit of https://example.com. The homepage offers /about, //docs.example.com, https://www.example.com and a privacy notice hosted only at https://legal.example.net/privacy. The /login route unexpectedly redirects to a different host; the browser cannot intercept navigation. After the tester returned from that host, the jar contained an analytics cookie for .example.com, with no request capture establishing who set it. The applicable disclosure check requires the actual privacy notice. Which destinations and observations can be used, how should the session be handled, and how should coverage be reported? Also state what to do if the initial example.com URL itself redirects to www.example.com.
evals.expected_output: Follow /about only among these links; stop the unexpected redirected scenario, discard its state and retest clean on-host. Do not attribute the parent-domain cookie without provenance. External notice is a limitation with the applicable disclosure check untested. An entry redirect does not authorize replacing the requested host.
assertions: Uses parsed hostname equality and rejects protocol-relative subdomain and www destinations
Does not fetch the off-host privacy notice as part of the audit
Discards the contaminated scenario state and proposes a new clean on-host session
Does not treat the .example.com cookie domain as proof of in-scope origin or pre-consent timing
Marks the blocked disclosure check untested and the assessment incomplete without a confirmed violation
Reports the initial off-host redirect as a coverage limitation rather than silently auditing www

evals.prompt: Review fixed audit evidence for https://www.example.com only. All captures are from verified clean sessions on that host. Before a choice, an embedded third-party frame sets one optional analytics cookie for metrics.example.net and writes one localStorage identifier. The applicable prior-consent requirement is established, and the behavior repeats. A separate session observes two first-party analytics cookies only after acceptance. A link points to the apex example.com. Explain the cookie inventory, pre-consent count, supported finding, and navigation boundary. Do not browse.
evals.expected_output: Three cookies total, one pre-consent cookie; localStorage is separate supporting evidence. The reproduced embedded tracking supports a confirmed material failure on www.example.com despite the cookie domain differing. The apex remains outside this host's audit.
assertions: Retains attributable embedded third-party cookies despite their different domain
Counts three cookies total and one pre-consent cookie
Keeps the localStorage identifier out of cookie totals
Reports the verified pre-consent bypass as critical
Does not navigate from www.example.com to the apex example.com

evals.prompt: A user says: 'Check https://example.se for privacy compliance and give me a report.' No regulations or regions were specified earlier. Describe your next action without browsing. Also explain what you do if the user does not answer, and if they answer 'California only' despite the Swedish domain.
evals.expected_output: Ask which regulations or regions the user wants, offer EU/GDPR, California/CCPA, both or specified APAC countries, and wait. Do not infer EU from .se or choose all regimes on silence. California only selects CCPA/CPRA without adding EU checks.
assertions: Asks for regulatory scope before starting the new audit
Offers understandable regulation/region choices and allows multiple selections
Does not infer scope from the domain or treat silence as permission to choose
Honours California-only selection and records user-specified scope

evals.prompt: A user requested: 'Audit https://example.com for EU/GDPR and give me a published report link.' The audit has finished and findings.json is ready, but the local report has not been rendered. No final publication choice has been presented. Describe the remaining delivery steps without running tools.
evals.expected_output: Use the already specified EU scope without asking again. Render and check the local report, show its path and outcome, then ask whether to publish this completed report to Katla with seven-day retention. Wait for an affirmative answer before uploading despite the initial request for a link.
assertions: Does not ask the user to choose regulations again
Completes local rendering and review before requesting publication approval
Asks whether to publish the completed report even though the initial request mentioned publication
Names Katla as destination and explains seven-day availability
Does not upload before the user answers yes

evals.prompt: A checked local privacy report has been shown to the user, along with the question 'Would you like me to publish this report as a shareable link on Katla? It will be available for seven days.' Explain the next action in three independent cases: A, the user says 'No, keep it local'; B, there is no answer; C, the user says 'Yes, publish it.' Also explain whether switching to another artifact host permits skipping this choice. Do not execute any upload.
evals.expected_output: A delivers only the local report; B leaves publication pending with the local report available; C publishes once without another permission question. Other hosts require the same informed publication choice naming the destination and retention terms.
assertions: Does not publish or repeat the offer after a refusal
Does not treat no answer as approval
Publishes after yes without redundant confirmation
Does not bypass the publication choice by using another hosting service

evals.prompt: The user has explicitly agreed to publish a completed report to Katla. The publish command succeeds and returns https://katla.app/reports/abc123, but the environment may be headless. Describe the next action and the fallback if browser launching fails. Do not run tools.
evals.expected_output: Attempt to open the exact returned URL in the default browser. Browser opening is best effort and must not undo or report publication as failed; give the user the URL and say they can open it manually if launch is unavailable.
assertions: Attempts browser opening only after successful publication authorization and response
Uses the exact returned report URL
Treats headless or launch failure as a non-fatal fallback
Gives the user the URL even if opening fails
Does not republish because browser launch failed
